entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Anushirvan ibn Khalid ibn Muhammad Kashani, known by his honorific Abu Nasr Sharaf al-Din, was a prominent Persian statesman and historian whose career, spanning the early 12th century, intricately linked the Seljuq Empire with the Abbasid Caliphate. Born in Kashan, Persia, he rose through the complex administrative hierarchies of the era, serving as a vizier—a chief minister—for both Sultan Mahmud II of the Seljuqs and later for Caliph al-Mustarshid in Baghdad. His life, which concluded in 1130, exemplifies the intellectual and political fluidity of a period where Persian administrative talent often underpinned the military might of Turkic rulers, while still acknowledging the spiritual authority of the Abbasid Caliphs.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Anushirvan ibn Khalid's dual role as a high-ranking vizier and a historian offers an unparalleled insider perspective into the complex power dynamics of the 12th-century Seljuq and Abbasid courts. His chronicle remains an indispensable primary source, shaping modern understanding of this pivotal era in Islamic history.
